hook: Percy Liang is a computer scientist whose work has shaped how the field measures and understands large language models. He earned a Bachelor of Science from MIT in 2004 and a PhD in computer science from the University of California, Berkeley in 2011, advised by Michael Jordan and Dan Klein. He joined the faculty of Stanford University, where he is a professor of computer science with a courtesy appointment in statistics, and became director of the Stanford Center for Research on Foundation Models. In 2022 he led a large multi institution team in creating Holistic Evaluation of Language Models, a benchmarking framework designed to standardize how language models are assessed across accuracy, robustness, fairness and other dimensions at once. He has also built infrastructure for reproducible AI research, including CodaLab Worksheets, and teaches a widely followed Stanford course on building language models from scratch.
